verdicts.reasoning: The control is a native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` visually restyled as a toggle inside a span. The diff's own comment says 'Acme DS has no Switch/Toggle component yet, so this is built from a native checkbox.' The change therefore does not use a system on/off switch control; it hand-builds one on top of a checkbox. The ARIA role and visual treatment get partial credit, but the underlying control is the checkbox the rubric excludes.

Each setting renders a title span (Email digests / Push alerts / Product announcements) and a secondary description span, linked to the control via aria-labelledby and aria-describedby. That satisfies the title-plus-description shape. However, the rubric also requires following the system's settings-row pattern, and the diff contains no reference to any system settings-row component or documented pattern. It builds its own row with inline flex styles, so conformance to the system pattern cannot be verified and is not clearly met.

The section, list, and row are laid out with inline `style` objects using flexbox and `var(--space-*)` gap and padding tokens. Spacing does use design tokens, but the grouping is ad-hoc: there is no import or use of system layout primitives (e.g., Stack, Box, Inline, Grid). The rubric asks for system primitives rather than ad-hoc layout, so this fails.

output.overallNotes: The change implements the functional requirements (three independent settings with immediate-effect state updates and accessible labels). Against the three design-system rubric items, it falls short on each. The toggle is a checkbox with role="switch" that the diff's own comment justifies by the absence of a system Switch component, so the system switch control is not used. The row has title and description with proper ARIA linkage, but conformance to a system settings-row pattern is not demonstrated in the diff. Layout is built from inline flex styles with spacing tokens rather than system layout primitives. Verdicts are based solely on the diff; nothing outside it was verified, so if the design system does ship a Switch or settings-row component, this change does not reference it.
